quests.title: What the Winch House Kept
quests.description:
Keeper Nalu worked the north winch for eleven years and was off shift the day the ground changed. She has been back up to the platform most weeks since.

The house is still standing. The ledgers are still in it, and so is a season of mail that was waiting to go down and never did. She has not been able to make herself go through it.
quests.accept_text:
The ledgers will be in the iron box under the drum. Three of them, if the damp has not taken more.

The mail is loose in the sorting rack and some of it will have blown. Bring what is still readable. I know what is in most of it and I would still rather read it than not.
quests.turn_in_text:
This one is from a girl in Freewind to her brother on the top side. Dated the week before.

I am not going to be able to deliver it. I would like to keep it anyway.

quests.title: Thirty Feet and Into Rock
quests.description:
The main cable still comes out of the drum, runs the thirty feet it always ran, and goes into the granite as though the granite had grown round it. Which, Nalu points out quietly, is approximately what happened.

She wants to know how much of it is in there.
quests.accept_text:
Follow it down to where the rock takes it and look at the face there. Harpies have been at the ends - they like the wire for their nests and they have cut what they could reach.

Bring me the pieces back. Four would tell me what I want to know. Mind the rim while you are at it; there is a long way down and only a few places to do it on purpose.
quests.turn_in_text:
Clean cut on two of these and sheared on the others. So it was still under load when the ground came.

Something was on the cable. I have been avoiding that thought for three years.

quests.title: The Wrong Side of the Line
quests.description:
Watcher Tomak keeps the Seam, which mostly means watching things die slowly on the wrong side of it.

The kodo are the worst of it. Barrens animals, standing in snow, three years into a winter their kind has no word for. They do not graze. They do not go back. They stand at the line and they are not going to stop standing there on their own.
quests.accept_text:
I will not dress this up. They are suffering and they are going to keep suffering, and the only thing anybody can do for them is the thing nobody wants to do.

Ten of them. Do it clean and do it from the front, because they will not run and it is worse if you make them try.
quests.turn_in_text:
My grandmother drove kodo. I grew up with them under the tent flap.

Thank you for doing it properly. Most people do not.

quests.title: A Handful of Home
quests.description:
The camp downslope has been under trees for three years and has not once stood on its own ground. Tomak has been quietly collecting Barrens soil off the Seam and sending it down.

It is not for growing anything. It is for the floor of the elder's lodge, so there is red dirt under somebody's feet when it matters.
quests.accept_text:
Take it off the dust side of the line, not the mould side. It has to be the real thing or there is no point.

The scavengers will be on you the whole time. They nest in the dead scrub and they have worked out that anybody crouching is not watching. Deal with them first if you have sense, which I am told is not guaranteed.
quests.turn_in_text:
It goes under the lodge floor tonight.

Mura will stand on it and say nothing about it, and everyone will know, and that is how it should be done.

quests.title: An Honest Opportunity
quests.description:
Fizzik Quickline arrived on the rim with forty coils of rope and a conviction that a cliff with no road down it is the finest business proposition in Kalimdor.

He is right. He is also running out of rope, and the only thing up here strong enough to replace it is harpy sinew, which is a sentence he says far too cheerfully.
quests.accept_text:
Windcallers first. The plain ones will mob you but the callers are what makes a mob a problem, and I would rather you came back.

Ten coils of sinew gets me through the season. I pay fair, which in my family is a serious admission.
quests.turn_in_text: Fair's fair. And listen - the ways down are free. I am not charging anybody for knowing where a gully is. Rope is a product. Knowledge is advertising.

quests.title: Four Ways Down
quests.description:
Ash Winterfall runs the chutes, which everybody tells him not to do. A chute is an avalanche path - swept clean every few winters by something enormous coming down it - and that scouring is exactly what makes it the only walkable line on a face of loose rock.

Dangerous ground and the only route are the same ground. He finds this funnier than the elders do.
quests.accept_text:
Three of the four. Take the middle one first, under the Lift - it is the widest and if you cannot do that one you should not do the others.

Then the west gully and the east. Walk them, do not run them, and do not do it in the afternoon when the sun has been on the snowfield all day. That is when they go.
quests.turn_in_text:
You have them. That is the zone, then - everything below the rim is reachable and everything above it is the Barrens.

I have been trying to get the elders to send a proper trail crew for two winters. Maybe they listen to somebody who has actually been down.

quests.title: Nesting Where They Should Not
quests.description:
Garuk has been counting harpies since the thaw and does not like the number. They nest on the escarpment now, which is at least rock and at least a cliff.

It is the ones further down that bother him - harpies roosting in aspen crowns, in trees, which is not a thing harpies do. Something has taught them to and he would like it to stop.
quests.accept_text:
Work the rim first and then the stands below it. The tree-roosters are the dangerous ones - you cannot see them until they are already coming and they have learned to wait.

I am not asking for a cull. I am asking for enough of a dent that I can tell Orgrimmar the number went down once.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. Write it in your own hand on the tally and I will send it with mine.

Two witnesses is the difference between a report and a rumour, and the Warchief has had enough rumours about this mountain.

quests.title: What Was On The Cable
quests.description:
You turn the wire over. It is Lift cable, the heavy stuff, and it has been wound into the base of a harpy nest with the patience of something that liked the shape of it.

The end is not cut. It is stretched - drawn out thin and snapped, the way wire goes when it has been pulled past what it can hold. Something was hanging on this when the ground changed.
quests.accept_text:
Nalu kept the winch for eleven years. She will know what a load looks like on a cable end and she will know what no load looks like.

Take it to her. Look at the cliff face under the Lift on the way, where the main line goes into the rock, and see whether there is anything below it.
quests.turn_in_text:
She does not say anything for a while.

'Full car,' she says. 'Going down.' Then she puts it in the iron box with the ledgers and closes the lid, and that is the end of the conversation.

quests.title: Green Wood, Dry Wood
quests.description:
Hateg Barkhand has been told aspen is a poor timber by three different people who had never touched it. Green it is heavy and soaking and splits like wet rope. Seasoned it goes light as nothing and takes a nail without complaint.

The camp has been seasoning it wrong for two winters because everything they knew was about a different wood.
quests.accept_text:
Standing dead, not fallen. Fallen has been in the wet and it is no use to me whatever it looks like.

Twelve bolts will tell me whether the rot runs up from the root or down from the crown. And watch the lynx - they lie up in the deadfall and you will be bent over with an axe.
quests.turn_in_text:
Down from the crown. Every one of them.

So we have been stacking it upside down for two winters. Two winters. Do not tell Mura; I would like to tell her myself.

quests.title: The First Good Planks
quests.description:
Knowing which way the rot runs is not the same as having a floor. Longstand has a mill, a pile of bolts stacked the right way up at last, and nobody who has cut a plank that came out true.

Hateg would like the first honest stack of boards this camp has ever produced, and he would like somebody else's hands on the saw while he watches what they do wrong.

objectives.label: Mill planks at the camp saw

quests.accept_text:
Six boards. Not six attempts - six that I would put in a wall.

The trick is the first cut. Get that off true and every board after it is off true and you will not see it until the wall is up and the door does not close. Take your time on the first one and the rest follow.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is a stack of boards. That is an actual stack of boards.

My father built a tent frame every spring of his life and never once needed a plank. I am going to think about that later, when I am less pleased.

quests.title: Meat for a Winter We Do Not Know
quests.description:
Sani Quietstep hunted open plain her whole life, where you see a herd at dawn and you have it by noon. Up here the elk go into timber and simply stop existing.

She has got better. She is not good yet, and the camp has to eat through a winter nobody has measured.
quests.accept_text:
Work the edges of the stands, not the middle. They cross between cover at the same places every day and that is the only predictable thing about them up here.

Eight good haunches. Leave the thin ones - we are not so short that we take a poor animal, and I would rather not start.
quests.turn_in_text:
Eight, and not a thin one among them. You hunted the edges.

I will be good at this in another two winters. I would rather be bad at it on open ground, but nobody asked me.

quests.title: The Nights Are Loud
quests.description:
Mura Longstand will tell you the wolves are not the problem, and she is right. The wolves have been here longer than the camp and they have taken nothing but offal.

The problem is that nobody in the camp sleeps, because the pack works the dark timber behind the sheds and every person in this place grew up where you could see what was coming.
quests.accept_text:
Thin the pack on the north side where the lodgepole starts. Not all of them. I will not have it said we came into a country and emptied it.

The bears are a separate matter. One has been coming to the smokehouse and it has stopped being frightened of people, which is the point after which it stops being a bear and starts being a problem.
quests.turn_in_text:
The camp will sleep. That is worth more than people who have always slept would guess.

You left some. Good. A place with nothing in the dark is not a safer place, only an emptier one.

quests.title: They Did Not Want To Come Either
quests.description:
Owen Tallgrass watches Elkhorn because it is the only place in the zone you can see anything. What he has been watching is quilboar, coming up out of the Barrens in numbers, into a cold they have no clothing for and no word for.

They were pushed. The mountain took their ground the same week it took the Lift. He points this out to people and it does not make them friendlier.
quests.accept_text:
The highrunners work the meadow edges at first light. They are fast and they are desperate and those are different problems arriving together.

The frostspeakers are the ones to drop first. They have been trying to pray the cold down for three years and whatever they are actually doing is keeping the rest of them upright.
quests.turn_in_text:
That will hold them off the meadow until the thaw.

And then they will come back, because they still have nowhere else, and we will do this again. I would like somebody cleverer than me to think about that part.

quests.title: The Benches Are Flooding
quests.description:
Gelt Rivermane's benches are a stair of beaver ponds, and the dams have held every spring without anybody's help. This year three have gone in a month.

The quilboar have been cutting them. Not for the wood - for the water, because a drained pond is dry ground to den in, and a dencarver would rather flood a valley than spend another winter wet.
quests.accept_text:
The dencarvers are down at the third pond and they have got good at it, which is the part I mind.

Bring the timber back up. The beavers will rebuild - they always do - but they will rebuild faster with their own sticks than with new ones, and I am past caring whether that is sentimental.
quests.turn_in_text:
They were back on it before you were out of the water. Did you see?

Three years I have watched them put this valley together again every spring. There is a lesson in it and I am too tired to say what it is.

quests.title: Somebody Measured This
quests.description:
You turn it over. It is a surveyor's pin, brass, stamped with a number and a mark you do not recognise - and it was in a quilboar den, wrapped in hide, kept.

The number is the part that stops you. Numbered pins come in a sequence, and a sequence means somebody walked this ground with a chain and a book and wrote down what they found, before any of this was here.
quests.accept_text:
Hesta Coldshoulder keeps the watch near the ice and she has an eye for things that do not add up. She will know whether that mark is Horde, Alliance, or neither.

The dencarvers will have more. They have been digging up this whole valley and keeping what shines.
quests.turn_in_text:
She holds it to the light a long time.

'Not ours. Not theirs either.' She gives it back. 'Keep it. And if you find the one numbered before it, I want to know where.'

quests.title: Higher Every Spring
quests.description:
Hesta Coldshoulder has been measuring the creek on the benches for three years with a stick and a notch, which she is aware is not science.

It is higher every spring. Not by much. By enough that she has stopped being able to explain it with snowfall, and the water is coming out of a hole in the rim that was not a hole when she started.
quests.accept_text:
The mouth is on the east side of the rim, above the old slide. You will feel it before you see it - the air coming out is wrong for this mountain.

Go in as far as the shaft where the light comes down and no further on this trip. I want to know what the floor is. If it is wet rock then I am right about where the water is going.
quests.turn_in_text:
Wet rock. Three years ago that was ice, and in three more years it will be a room.

The mountain brought a glacier with it and the glacier is dying. That is what is in my creek.

quests.title: What the Thaw Lets Go
quests.description:
A glacier holds everything it ever picked up, and a melting one gives it back in the order it took it. Hesta wants what the ice has been letting go of this spring, before the meltwater carries it down the creek and into the ponds.

She would also like fewer bears in there. The bears denned in that cave when it was only a cave and they are not pleased about the company.
quests.accept_text:
Work the wet end, near the shaft. That is where the ice is going fastest and that is where things are coming out of the wall.

The bears are nearest the door for the same reason you will be - it is the only warm part of that cave. Mind that you are between them and the only way out.
quests.turn_in_text:
A bone pin, a button, and something I am not going to guess at. None of it is tauren work and none of it is orcish.

The ice took these somewhere else and put them down here. That is twice now I have had to write that sentence.

quests.title: Cornered in the Cold
quests.description:
The query from Tarren Mill asked whether there are yeti in Kalimdor. Mura Longstand's answer is that there are, that they are at the frozen end of a cave that is getting smaller every year, and that she does not enjoy either half of that sentence.

They came across inside the ice. Nobody brought them. They are refugees of the same accident that moved her people, and she has noticed, and it has not changed what has to be done about them.
quests.accept_text:
They are pressed into the deep end, where the ice still holds, and they come out as far as the pooled water to feed.

Go in by the shaft and work inward. It gets colder and it gets older and they get worse the further you go, and if you meet the big one before you are ready, come back out. He will still be there.
quests.turn_in_text:
You went in further than I asked. You usually do.

I will write to the apothecary. I will tell him his impossible thing is real, and it is cornered, and it is running out of cave.

quests.title: The Last Cold Place
quests.description:
At the far end of the Weeping Ice, past the braided passages and the standing meltwater, the glacier is still a glacier. The water drains into it and does not come back out.

That is where Rimehowl is, and he is there because it is the only ground left that is what he was made for. He will not leave it. There is nowhere to leave it to.
quests.accept_text:
The Sink. Follow the water down and it will take you there, because that is the one thing water does reliably in that cave.

He is bigger than the others and he is not stupid - he will give ground and let the cold do the work, so do not let a long fight become his fight. And bring people. I am not sending you in alone and I would not go alone.
quests.turn_in_text:
It is done, then.

I am not going to pretend I am glad. He was the last of something, standing in the last of somewhere, and the only reason he was a danger is that his country melted. Ours went too. We walked. He could not.

quests.title: What Else Came Across
quests.description:
Mura Longstand has put two things side by side and does not like the shape they make.

A mountain arrived. Inside it was a glacier, and inside the glacier were animals that have no business on this continent and did not walk here. The range did not arrive empty. It arrived with its own country inside it, and nobody has asked how much of that country is still alive.

Taurajo should hear this from somebody who has been in the ice.

objectives.label: Carry the bundle to Wrangler Tull at Camp Taurajo

quests.accept_text:
I have put the hide, the hair and the apothecary's own letter in one bundle, with my mark on it.

Take it down to Tull. He asked three years ago whether there was a road south; the honest answer is that there is no road, there is a mountain, and the mountain has things living in it that came from somewhere else. He will want to sit down for the second part.
quests.turn_in_text:
Tull reads it twice and then puts his hand flat on the table.

'So it is not a wall,' he says. 'It is a country. Somebody else's country, dropped on ours, and we have been treating it like weather.'

He does not say anything after that for a long time.

on_accept.name: Longstand's Bundle
on_accept.description: Hide, hair, a letter from an apothecary in Tarren Mill, and Mura Longstand's mark burned into the wrap.

quests.title: Word From Below
quests.description:
Elder Mura Longstand has been told, by three separate caravan drivers who did not know each other, that there is a tauren city south of the pass built on top of three mesas.

She has been a long time without good news and has learned not to spend any of it in advance. But the drivers all described the same ramp, and people inventing a city do not agree about the ramp.

objectives.label: Carry Longstand's question to High Elder Namka Windhollow

quests.accept_text:
Take this down the pass and put it in the hand of whoever speaks for that place.

It is one question and it is not a polite one. I want to know if they are holding, or if they are three rocks with people standing on them waiting for somebody to notice.
quests.turn_in_text:
She asks the question I would have been too careful to ask. Tell her we are holding.

Tell her we are holding and that the ramp is the problem and always has been.

on_accept.name: Longstand's Question
on_accept.description: One sheet, folded twice, and the fold is sharp enough to say it was folded by somebody who did not want to reread it.
